header_sentences: See Bring forth, Draw away, Guidance, Introduce, and Lead into.

contexts.text: It is a heavenly arcanum, that man is led (by the Lord) both by the fallacies of the senses, and by cupidities...
The Angels do indeed lead, but they only minister; for it is the Lord alone who rules man through Angels and Spirits.
As man is such that he is not content to be led by the Lord; but desires to be led by self and the world, or from proprium, it here treats of the proprium which was conceded to him.
The love of self is attended with this, - that they do not want to be led by the Lord, but by self...
So long as Spirits suppose that they lead themselves... they cannot have perception.
Then also he is led through ways of which he himself is ignorant, even to the designated place.
Therefore they are among the less useful ones; for they suffer themselves to be led equally by the evil and the good; and they suffer much from the evil.
The Spirits... could not withhold themselves from leading (the infants) to think and to speak...
Such is the temptation of the infants... to accustom them... to not suffering themselves to be led by another, except by the Lord alone. HH 343.
For the least things... with man are foreseen by the Lord, and are provided for his future state to eternity; and this for his good, in so far... as the man suffers himself to be led by the Lord.
Good, into which God leads him who is in temptations... But it is the evil with man... which leads into temptation.

The evil Spirits with a man... infuse into him their cupidities and their persuasions, and thus lead him wherever they want. But the Angels... insinuate into him affections of good and truth, and thus lead him by freedom, not whither they want, but whither the Lord pleases. Hence it is evident... that it is slavery to be led by the devil, and that it is freedom to be led by the Lord.
The more exquisitely (the Angels) perceive that they are led by the Lord... the more they are in freedom.

Although there were so many (Angels), they all thought and spoke as one... and this because no one wanted... to lead the choir: he who does this is of himself dissociated in a moment. But they suffered themselves to be led mutually by each other; thus all in singular and in general by the Lord...
For he who suffers himself to be led by the Lord, never intends and thinks anything else (than what is good).
When man is being regenerated... he is led by the Lord through many states. Signified.

They who are in the affection of good from which is not truth... suffer themselves to be led into any evil and also falsity; provided there is induced on the evil the likeness of good, and on the falsity the likeness of truth.

The good of love to God, and the good of charity towards the neighbour... suffer themselves to be led by the Lord... Otherwise those who are in the love of self and of the world; these do not suffer themselves to be led and bent by the Lord, and to the Lord; but resist severely; for they want to lead themselves...

These are not such as do much from themselves and from proprium; but they suffer themselves to be led by others; thus to good by the Angels, and to evil by evil Spirits; which also shines forth from the historicals here concerning Laban.

For the Angels see and perceive with a man who is being regenerated all the changes of his state... and according to them and by means of them they, from the Lord, lead to good, in proportion as the man suffers himself to be led.
For it is foreseen by the Lord... how a man will suffer himself to be led by the Lord.
If they had believed... that all good and truth are from the Lord, they would have suffered themselves to be led by the Lord...
So that he can, if he chooses, be led from Hell to Heaven, and through Heaven to the Lord.

The Lord leads everyone by his affections, and thus bends by a silent Providence; for he leads by freedom... When, therefore, man has been led to good in freedom, then truths are accepted and implanted... He who has been regenerated... if he reflects upon his past life, will then discover that he has been led by many things of his thought, and by many things of his affection.
Man is led by the Lord in spiritual life by almost the like things as those by which a man leads others in civil life. Example(s).
Therefore infants are led by the Lord by means of infants and Angels from the Lord.
(Then) Spirits from Hell led those (of the Ancient Church).
For good is what teaches and leads; and truth is what is taught and led.
Widows = those who... nevertheless long to be led through good. Illustrated.
It here treats of those who are being instructed in truths and led to good by the Lord.
An orphan = those who... long to be led through truth to good; and a widow = those who... long to be led through good to truth.

The Lord is called the Father (of the orphans), because He leads them like a father; and this through truth into good... The Lord is called the Judge (of the widows), because He leads them; and this through good into truth... For by a judge is signified a leader.
All those with whom the voluntary interiors have been terminated, are elevated to Heaven; for the influent Divine can lead them...
They who are being regenerated... choose, from freedom, to be led by the Lord as to willing and thinking...
For to be led by the Lord is freedom; for he is led in good, from good, to good.
No one can be gifted with this peace, except him who is led by the Lord...
He is thus led, through degrees, to good.

The truths of faith, inrooted through the affection of truth, are the plane into which the Angels operate; and therefore those who have not this plane cannot be led by the Angels; but suffer themselves to be led by Hell.
Suffers himself to be led by means of reasonings equally by evil and by good Spirits.
In freedom man must be withdrawn from evil, and be led to good.
(How the Angels lead man. See Angel.)
He is (then) said to be withdrawn from sensuous things.

For the man who is led by the Lord is in freedom itself; and thus in delight and bliss itself; goods and truths are appropriated to him; the affection and longing to do what is good is given him: and then nothing is more happy to him than to perform uses; the perception of good is given him; and also the sensation of it; and intelligence and wisdom are given him; and all these things as his own; for he is then a recipient of the Lord's life.
Whereas the affection of the latter love inflows from the Lord, who does not command, but leads.
For they do not know that those who are led by the Lord want nothing more than to do good works; and think nothing less than about merit through them...

The Lord does not compel man to receive what inflows from Himself; but leads in freedom; and, in proportion as man allows, through freedom leads to good: thus the Lord leads man according to his delights; and also according to fallacies and the principles taken thence; but He gradually leads him from these; and this appears to the man as if from himself...
It was shown... that each thing of his life had been led by the Lord; and that otherwise he would have precipitated himself into the most frightful Hell...
He took a daughter of Levi () = conjunction with good. To take... namely, to wife = conjunction.
There are evil Spirits with these (preachers)... who lead them.
When a man knows these truths, and wants to do according to them, he is then led by the Lord...

For those with whom immediate Divine influx has been conjoined with mediate, suffer themselves to be led by the Lord; but those with whom these influxes have not been conjoined, lead themselves, and love this.
Derives its origin. AC 7272.
Multiplied into each other.

God did not lead them by the way of the Philistines () = that it was provided by the Divine that they should not pass to the truth of faith which is not from good... For to lead, when by God, = Providence.

God led the people about by the way of the wilderness () = that from the Divine auspices they were brought to confirm the goods and truths of faith through temptations. God led = Providence; or, what is the same, the Divine auspices.
To lead them in the way () = the Divine auspices. (For) to lead in the way, when said of Jehovah, = Providence...
He dragged his [chariot] in heaviness () = resistance and impotence.
In Thy mercy Thou hast led Thy people () = the Divine influx with those who had abstained from evils, and thus had received good. To lead in mercy = to receive the Divine...

In Thy virtue Thou hast conducted to the habitation of Thy holiness () = that the Divine power of the Lord has elevated them to Heaven, into the Divine there. To lead in virtue = ... to elevate from Divine power.
That those who are in natural good and not in spiritual good cannot possibly be led by any influx from Heaven. References.
That with those who are led by the Lord all things inflow, even to the last of life, both intellectual and voluntary. References.
For he who acts from truth leads himself; whereas he who acts from good is led by the Lord. Signified.
For the order in which man is led by the Lord is through the willing of man, consequently through good...

By to live according to order, is here meant to be led by the Lord through good; whereas by not yet living according to order, is to be led through truth; and, when man is led through truth, the Lord does not appear; and therefore the man then also walks in darkness, in which he does not see good. It is otherwise when man is led through good; he then sees in light.

When a man does what is good for the sake of himself... the interiors are closed, and he cannot be led through Heaven by the Lord; but he is led by himself. The love determines by whom a man is led; for everyone is led by his love: he who loves himself more than his neighbour leads himself; but he who loves good is led by good, consequently by the Lord from whom is good.
Everyone must be led to... charity through the truth of faith.

When a man has been regenerated... he is led by the Lord through good; and no longer through truth... All in Heaven are so led; for this is according to Divine order... If they were to think and act from truth... they would be... led by themselves, and not by the Lord. Explained. AC 8539:2.
The Sabbath = a state of peace... in which man is led by the Lord through good. If man were then to lead himself, even by truth, he would dissipate the state of peace...
Those who are in the affection of truth for the sake of the uses of life... are led by the Lord through good...
The life of Heaven is to be led by the Lord through good...
The Divine Providence differs from every other leading... in this, - that it continually... leads to salvation...
In the first state... the man is led by the Lord through truth... AC 8701. AC 8731:end.
Man is then led by the Lord through good. AC 8702:end, Described.
In the other life everyone is led according to his will which he had procured in the world.
What it is to be led by the Lord through truth, and what through good. References. AC 8750:end.
The man who is being regenerated is first led by the Lord through truth, and afterwards through good. References. AC 8935:2. AC 9096:end. AC 9274:2. AC 9294:3.
One man leads another according to his ruling love.
For it is slavery... to be led by those in Hell; and freedom to be led by the Lord. References. AC 8988:2. AC 10409. AE 409:9, Signified.
As soon as the good of love has been implanted... the man is led by the Lord according to the laws of order (in Heaven); thus in peace. Signified.
Hence he who is led by the Lord thinks nothing at all about reward; and still does good to the neighbour from the heart.
In the same proportion the man is not led through truths, but through good; consequently, in the same proportion he is led by the Lord.
Men of holiness = those who are led by the Lord...
To bring thee to the place which I have prepared () = introduction into Heaven...
There are thousands and thousands of arcana... through which man is led by the Lord... into the life of Heaven.
To lead into the way () = to teach truth.
Without doctrine for a directress and leader.
Heavenly freedom is to be led by the Lord... but infernal freedom is to be led by the devil.
How the Lord leads man through the truths of faith, or through faith; namely, (that it is) through the good of love with him. Explained.
A cunning man... is delighted to lead others by such things...
When man is withdrawn from sensuous things... he is withdrawn or elevated into the light of his spirit.
He then leads him by his love wherever he wants...
In (the first) state, man is led through truth to good, thus partly by himself; but in the latter one... he is led by good; that is, by the Lord through good. Signified.
They who suffer themselves to be led by the Lord... are in the sphere of Divine good...
For if a man is not in the good of innocence, he is not led by the Lord; but by himself: and he who is led by himself is led by Hell.

By the Sabbath is signified a state of the conjunction of man with the Lord; thus a state when man is led by the Lord, and not by himself; which state is when he is in good. For to be led by the Lord, and not by self, is to turn away the foot from the Sabbath; not to do our own wills; not to do our own ways; not to find our own desire; and not to speak a word ().
Profaning it = to be led by self and our own loves, and not by the Lord.

It is to be known that to be led by self and to be led by the Lord are two opposite things; for he who is led by self is led by his own loves; thus by Hell... and he who is led by the Lord, is led by the loves of Heaven... He who is led by these loves, is withdrawn from his Own loves; and he who is led by his Own loves, is withdrawn from the loves of Heaven...
For all who acknowledge God under a human form... are led: the rest cannot be led...
To make to ascend from the land of Egypt... = to lead themselves. Explained.
To be a disciple of the Lord = to be led by Him, and not by self; thus by the goods and truths which are from the Lord; and not by the evils and falsities which are from man.
The Divine which will lead. Signified, Explained.
Spiritual death for those who are led by themselves and their own loves, and not by the Lord. Signified. (by doing work on the Sabbath day).

Priests must teach men the way to Heaven, and also lead them: they must teach them according to the doctrine of their Church, and they must lead them to live according to it. The priests who... do not lead to the good of life, and thus to the Lord, are evil shepherds.
Priests must teach the people, and must lead through truths to the good of life... Life 39.
When they were withdrawn from the body...
They who are in innocence... want to be led by the Lord, and not by self.

As innocence is to be led by the Lord, and not by self, all in Heaven... love to be led by the Lord; for they know that to lead one's self is to be led by proprium... and he who loves himself does not suffer himself to be led by another. HH 341. CL 414:end.
For in proportion as anyone is wise, he loves to be led by the Lord; or, what is the same, in proportion as anyone is led by the Lord, he is wise.
Man believes in the Divine when he wants to be led by the Divine.
The reason the Lord's yoke is easy... is that in proportion as a man resists evils... he is led by the Lord, and not by self.
And to be thus led by the Lord, from infancy to the last of life here, and afterwards to eternity, is the mercy which is meant.
All Spirits can be led wherever you please, provided they are kept in their reigning love...

Through Divine truths the Lord leads man to Heaven... In proportion, therefore, as a man abstains from evil, the Lord, from pure mercy, leads him through His Divine means; and this from infancy to the end of his life in the world, and afterwards to eternity...

In proportion as anyone is in celestial love, which is to love uses and goods... he is led by the Lord; because this love is that in which He is... But in proportion as anyone is in the love of self... he is led by self; and in proportion as anyone is led by self, he is not led by the Lord... To be led by self is to be led by one's own proprium...

This is especially the case when a man is led by the Lord; for he is then introduced into genuine truths... and into genuine goods... for the Lord then disposes all things of such a mind into the form of Heaven...
The will leads the understanding.
Therefore man is continually led by the Lord in freedom...
To be led by self they call slavery. Explained.
That... man is to be led and taught by the Lord from Heaven, through the Word, doctrine, and preachings from it; and this in all appearance as of himself. General article.

It is from appearance that man is led and taught by himself; and it is from Truth, that man is led and taught by the Lord alone. They who confirm... the appearance... cannot remove from themselves evils as sins... They are all interior idolaters; for they are worshippers of self and the world...
But they who confirm... the Truth, become worshippers of the Lord; for the Lord... gives them to perceive interiorly that they are not led and taught by themselves, but by the Lord.
That man is led and taught by the Lord alone. General article.
That man is led and taught by the Lord alone, means that he lives from the Lord alone; for the will of his life is led, and the understanding of his life is taught...
That man is led and taught by the Lord alone through the angelic Heaven and from it. General article.
That man is led through... Heaven, is from the appearance; but that he is led from it, is from the Truth. Explained.
That man is led by the Lord through influx... General article.
For to be led, and also to inflow, are said of... the will.
That every man is led of himself from his own love; and according to it by others... is known. He is led by the understanding and according to it only when... the will makes it...
That in externals man is led and taught by the Lord to all appearance as by himself. General article.
No one knows how the Lord leads and teaches man in his internals...

If man perceived and felt the Divine Providence, he would also be led by it; for the Lord leads all through His Divine Providence; and man does not lead himself, except apparently... and therefore if he were led with a living perception and sensation, he would not be conscious of life...
(Thus) man knows no otherwise than that he leads himself.
By His Divine Providence the Lord leads man silently; as a hidden stream... does a ship.
That the affections of the life's love of man are led by the Lord through His Divine Providence, and at the same time the thoughts, from which is human prudence. Explained.
It follows that unless the Lord leads man every moment... the man recedes from the way of reformation and perishes.
It is according to the laws of the Divine Providence for it to appear to man as if he leads himself; but the Lord foresees how he leads himself... DP 203.

They who acknowledge God and His Divine Providence... are averse to be led by themselves, and love to be led by the Lord. A sign that they are led by the Lord, is that they love the neighbour. But they who acknowledge nature and Own prudence... are averse to being led by the Lord, and love to be led by themselves...
It follows that unless man disposes as from his Own prudence all things which are of his function and life, he cannot be led and disposed from the Divine Providence...
Therefore, if you want to be led by the Divine Providence, use prudence, as a servant... who faithfully dispenses the goods of his lord...
Under Free, see this reference. SE 5797.

For man does not know whether he is led by the devil, or by the Lord. He who is led by the devil does uses for the sake of himself and the world; but he who is led by the Lord does uses for the sake of the Lord and Heaven... From this (alone) is the difference Known...
This is the good through which every man, even an evil man, is led by the Lord.

By these means the Lord leads the evil; but only from doing those things; and not from thinking and willing them. But by the former means the Lord leads the good; not only from doing those things, but also from thinking and willing them.
As these... look to God, and do no evil to the neighbour, they are led by the Lord; and they who are led are also taught...
That the evil are continually leading themselves into evils; and that the Lord is continually leading them away from evils. General article.
That an evil person, from himself, is continually leading himself more deeply into his evils. Explained.
That the Divine Providence with the evil is a continual permission of evil, to the end that there may be a continual withdrawal. Explained.
That the withdrawal is effected by the Lord in a thousand ways, even the most secret. Explained.

With an evil man there is no other... withdrawal than of the more grievous evils from the less grievous; whereas with a good man there is not only the... withdrawal of the more grievous evils, but also of the less grievous ones...
That the evil cannot be completely... led away from evils, and led into goods, so long as they believe Own intelligence to be everything... General article.
That man is thereby led away from evil; not by himself, but by the Lord. Explained.
He who believes in the Divine Providence is led away from evil; whereas he who does not believe in it, is not led away...
Thus they lead others (by their cupidities)...
Therefore He cannot lead man, except according to the laws of His Divine Providence.
The effect of conjunction is that the Lord turns the man's face to Himself, and then leads him; but the effect of separation is, that Hell turns the man's face to itself, and leads him.
With the evil the Lord provides by leading away from evils; but with the good He provides by leading to good...

Those want to be saved who acknowledge God, and are led by Him; and those do not want, who do not acknowledge God, and lead themselves... This the Lord sees, and still leads them; and He leads them according to the laws of His Divine Providence...
He shall lead to living fountains of waters () = He will lead through the truths of the Word to conjunction with Himself.
That man does not at all know that he is led by Spirits, and through Spirits.

One Spirit is led by others; and, successively, by others... and still the Spirit knows no otherwise than that he is leading himself... In like manner, also, a Spirit can be led by a man... SE 3117. a.
That he who is led by the Lord perceives in each thing he does whether it is of permission, of leave, or of good pleasure... Explained.
That he who is led by the Lord is blameless. Explained.
Spirits who are not led by the Lord, but who want to lead themselves (could not do right, however they acted).
That some are more easily led by the Lord. SE 2223.

It is as easy for the Lord to lead one as another; but as it pleases the Lord to lead according to order, it is more easy to lead him who is in order than him who is not in order; for he has first to be brought back into the way, or into order, which causes delay, to prevent his being broken.
That from the creation of the first man the Lord has led the human race. Explained.
That there are mere necessities through which man is led.
That man is marvellously led...
How man is led to good ends also, even by the evil. Explained.
For they are thus led through series of their cupidities...

For man to be led by the Lord, there must not be the least pertinacity in him. So much pertinacity, so much is there of the proprium of man; which is taken away by the Lord in those who are led by the Lord...
One who supposed that by a mental look directed into others, he could lead them... wherever he wanted; which is so common in the other life...
That man can never be led any better.

Spirits suppose that they could have been led otherwise; and thus could become better than they are... But I perceived in a spiritual idea that they never can be led better; so that there are necessities every moment of their lives... SE 3115.
For man also can thus almost similarly lead man in some particulars, when he knows his evil nature, or cupidity.
How one Spirit leads another both to think and to speak. (See Free.)

It is not conceded to any Spirit to teach man, nor consequently to lead him, except from cupidity; but the Lord alone wills to teach and lead man; which would not be possible if a Spirit had anything of the corporeal memory.
Spirits are indignant and complain, when they perceive that another is leading them... They care nothing when they are not noticing it; they then suppose that they are leading themselves...
A Spirit who said that he had led Paul.
Hence it was evident that in proportion as the external man acts as one with the internal, the man can be led by the Lord...

When they were turned to lower things, they wanted to lead all whom they saw... For in the other life the thoughts are communicated; and the one leads the other marvellously by means of the thoughts...

The Lord leads his will... so that he is affected with good; and leads his understanding, so that he is affected with truth... and in proportion as he learns truth... he is led by the Lord through it; for he who does not know what is good and true cannot be led by the Lord: a man is led through that which he knows: the Lord inflows into the things which he knows, and thus leads his affections and thoughts... (that is to say) the Lord leads him by means of those things which he learns from affection.
Thus the Lord leads men of the world by their Own affections.
(Thus) man is led by the Lord to foreseen ends by continual necessities; and still [he is led] by his freedom.
(Such) are led by means of Heaven by the Lord.

In proportion to the charity there is in the faith, he is led by the Lord; but in proportion as there is no charity in it, he is led by himself; and he who is led by himself, and not by the Lord, cannot think what is good; still less can he will and do good which in itself is good...
To lead (), when said of the Lord, = to illustrate.
Thy leaders () = those who teach.

From this it may be evident, that it is of the Divine omnipotence to lead man according to order; and this every moment, from the beginning of his life, even to eternity; and this according to the laws of order... that is to say, in so far as the man suffers himself to be led; that is, in so far as he does not want to be led by himself; for he who wants this, is in the same proportion carried against order. And as it is of the Divine omnipotence to lead according to order the man who wants to be led therefore it is not of the Divine omnipotence to lead anyone to Heaven who wants to lead himself... Hence it may be evident, that it is not of the Divine omnipotence to save those who do not want to be led according to order; for to be led according to order is to be led according to the laws of order... and therefore to lead according to these laws every moment and continually to eternity the man who wants to be led, is of the Divine omnipotence...
These things were represented by the... leading about of the sons of Israel in the wilderness.
VI. In proportion as a man is in these good affections, he is led by the Lord, and not by himself.
In proportion as a man lives religion, he is led by the Lord; and in proportion as he is led by the Lord, his works are good...
To deny one's self = not to be led by self, but by the Lord...

From these things it may be evident, that to follow the Lord = to be led by Him, and not by self; and no one else can be led by the Lord than he who is not led by self; and everyone is led by self who does not shun evils because they are contrary to the Word. Explained... Whereas, when evils have been removed... then the Lord enters... and leads him... AE 865:end.
Only abstain from evils as sins, and look to the Lord; and the Lord will teach and lead.

By the love of dominating, a man completely averts himself from the Lord... and thus can no longer be led by the Lord; but is led by his own proprium; and to be led by one's own proprium, is to be led by Hell. Man is led from Heaven, or else he is led from Hell; he cannot be led by both together. He is led from Heaven when he is led by the Lord; and he is led from Hell when he is led by himself...

That the Word is Divine holiness from inmosts to outermosts, is not evident to the man who leads himself, but to the man whom the Lord leads; for the man who leads himself sees only the external of the Word... whereas the man whom the Lord leads judges concerning the external of the Word from the Holy which is therein.

An Angel man is led by the Lord both from within and from without; but a devil man is led by himself from within, and by the Lord from without. An angel man is led by the Lord according to order; from within, from order; from without, to order: but a devil man is led by the Lord to order from without; but by himself contrary to order from within. An Angel man is continually led from evil by the Lord, and is led to good; but a devil man is also continually led from evil by the Lord; but from a more grievous to a less one; for he cannot be led to good... As an Angel man is led by the Lord, he is led by the civil law, by the moral law, and by the spiritual law, for the sake of the Divine in them. A devil man is led by the same laws; but for the sake of what is his own in them.

The ways through which the Lord leads man are much more involved and inextricable; both those through which the Lord leads a man by the Societies of Hell, and from them; and also those through which He leads a man by the Societies of Heaven, and more interiorly into them.

Through man's internal freedom, the Lord enters to man even into Hell, where he is; and through it leads him there; and, if he is willing to follow, leads him out thence, and introduces him into Heaven...
How the Lord inflows; and how man is thus led...

Thus and no otherwise can man be led by affection into affection... from the affection of truth and good, by leading, if he acknowledges the Divine Providence in each thing; and from the affection of evil and falsity, by permitting, if he does not acknowledge it.

Similar would it be if the Lord were to lead man by thoughts, immediately; and not by affections. Moreover, when a man is led by the Lord by affections, it appears to him as if he thinks from himself freely...
The good of love is that by which God leads man; and the truth of faith is that through which man is led. Explained.

(Those who are in faith alone) are such that they do not want to be led; but to lead: this is their delight; and therefore they cannot be led by the Lord; for the Lord leads through the affection of use...
Nay (the diabolical Spirits) lead (their thought).

For when the Lord is reforming and regenerating man, he leads in like manner his will and understanding; but by means of the will given him, and by means of the understanding given him, it appears as if the man himself is leading himself...
